dicas.texto: Boa observação! Quando comemos mais fatias do que tem em uma pizza inteira, a fração fica maior que 1. Que número representa quantas fatias foram comidas? E quantas fatias tem em uma pizza inteira?
Você está no caminho certo! O numerador é o total de fatias comidas (9), e o denominador é o número de fatias em uma pizza inteira (6). Digite esses números nas caixas da fração.
Quase lá! A fração correta usa 9 como numerador e 6 como denominador. Verifique se você digitou esses valores nas caixas certas.
Você está muito perto! Na caixa de cima (numerador), coloque 9. Na caixa de baixo (denominador), coloque 6. Isso representa exatamente o que o problema descreveu.
Pense: se cada unidade tem 6 partes iguais, quantas partes você precisa contar para chegar a 9/6? Comece do zero e vá contando!
Ótimo! Primeiro localize 1 (que é 6/6). Depois, continue contando mais 3 partes: 7/6, 8/6, 9/6. Marque exatamente nesse ponto.
Você está quase! 9/6 está exatamente na metade entre 1 e 1,5. Olhe as marcas invisíveis — a terceira após o 1 é o lugar certo.
Muito bem! Comece em 0, conte 6 partes até chegar em 1, depois mais 3: 7ª, 8ª, 9ª. Clique exatamente na 9ª marca — essa é a posição de 9/6.

dicas.texto: Think about what the whole unit is in this problem: one complete pizza.
Place the number of eaten slices above the number of slices that make one pizza.
Use the eaten slices for the top part and the slices in one pizza for the bottom part.
Count the eaten slices for the numerator, count the equal slices in one pizza for the denominator, and represent those two counts as a fraction.
The numerator tells how many parts are being counted or used.
Look for the quantity that describes the slices eaten, rather than the size of one pizza.
Read the sentence that says how many slices Rick and his friends ate.
Count the slices eaten in the story and enter that count in the top field.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole unit.
Identify the number of equal slices in a single pizza.
Do not use the total number of slices available in both pizzas; focus on one pizza.
Read how many slices each pizza was divided into and enter that number in the bottom field.
Remember that the top number of a fraction counts the parts being considered.
Use the quantity from the story that tells how many slices were eaten.
The upper field is not the number of slices in one pizza; it records the eaten slices.
Enter the count of all slices eaten into f1, the upper numeric field.
A fraction greater than one can also be described using whole units and a remaining fractional part.
Use the control that opens separate fields for the whole part and the fractional part.
The conversion control is labeled Convert and appears beside the fraction fields.
Select the Convert button once to reveal the mixed-number fields.
Compare the eaten amount with one whole pizza before choosing a location.
Count sixths along the number line, remembering that six sixths make one whole.
After reaching 1, continue three more sixth intervals toward 2.
Start at 0, move nine sixth-sized intervals, and place the point halfway between 1 and 2.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator represents more than one complete denominator-sized group.
Compare the numerator with the denominator and check whether the point lies to the right of 1.
There are enough sixths for one whole pizza and some sixths beyond it.
Confirm that the point is between 1 and 2 and that the numerator is larger than the denominator, then click Done.

exercicio.statement:

nodes.description: Aluno foca na contagem absoluta e ignora a necessidade de expressar como fração da unidade
nodes.instruction: You identified the total number of slices eaten, but the problem asks for the amount in pizzas. Compare the eaten slices with the slices in one whole pizza.

nodes.description: Aluno fixa no dado 'cada pizza tem 6 fatias' e responde isso como a fração
nodes.instruction: You noticed that one pizza has six slices, but the fraction must also show how many slices were eaten.

nodes.description: Aluno pensa que o denominador é o total de fatias disponíveis, não o tamanho da unidade
nodes.instruction: The denominator describes one whole pizza, not all the available pizzas. Use the number of slices in one pizza as the unit.

nodes.description: Aluno fixa no dado 'cada pizza tem 6 fatias' e responde isso como a fração
nodes.instruction: Six is the number of slices in one pizza, not the number of slices eaten. The numerator records the eaten slices.

nodes.description: Aluno foca na contagem absoluta e ignora a necessidade de expressar como fração da unidade
nodes.instruction: Nine is the number of slices eaten. The denominator must describe the equal parts in one whole pizza.

nodes.description: Aluno fixa no dado 'cada pizza tem 6 fatias' e responde isso como a fração
nodes.instruction: The upper field is the numerator, so it records the slices eaten. Six belongs in the denominator because it describes one whole pizza.

nodes.description: Aluno posiciona corretamente a fração que digitou, mas a fração está errada desde o início
nodes.instruction: Your point represents about two-thirds, which would come from reversing the relationship between the eaten slices and one whole pizza. Since the eaten amount is greater than one whole pizza, the point must be after 1.

nodes.description: Aluno trata a fração como número inteiro e posiciona além da escala da reta (0 a 2)
nodes.instruction: The number line measures pizzas, not individual slices. Six sixth intervals make 1 whole, so nine intervals stay between 1 and 2.

nodes.description: Aluno conta as marcas em vez dos intervalos, somando 1 a mais
nodes.instruction: You counted one sixth interval too many. Count the spaces between marks, starting with the first interval after 0.

nodes.description: Aluno associa 'comeram bastante' à metade e posiciona incorretamente
nodes.instruction: One-half is below 1, but the eaten amount is more than one whole pizza. The point must be to the right of 1.

nodes.description: Aluno simplifica mentalmente para 'cerca de 1 pizza' e ignora a parte fracionária
nodes.instruction: The amount is close to 1 but not exactly 1. Continue counting the remaining sixth intervals after the first whole pizza.
